$comment: What makes the generic case desk the reconciliation desk. Start it with DESK_CONFIG pointing at this file. Needs the settings-driven case desk engine. The bank (Meridian Trust Bank), its correspondent banks, its accounts and its entries are invented. The demo cases are fixed at the bank date 24 Nov 2026: start the bank with BANK_TODAY=2026-11-24.

desk.name: Reconciliation desk
desk.tagline: Unmatched items from each reconciliation run, the break item set beside the entry it was compared with, a proposed match or adjusting entry for each, a place to decide, and the register afterwards.

case.heading: THE BREAK
case.textHeading: The break, as the desk holds it
case.noTextShown: The desk holds no summary for this break. The agent reads the break from the reconciliation system.
case.noTextNote: No summary was supplied with this break. Work from the break the case names, read from the reconciliation system.
case.askPlaceholder: For example: why is LED-7203 not part of the match?
case.searchPlaceholder: Search by bank, break id, entry or account
case.demoNote: Demo data: the bank, its correspondent banks, its accounts and its entries are invented. Nothing here is a real ledger.
case.replyLabel: The reply (it is added to the break)
case.replyButton: Add the reply and draft again
case.replyNote: A reply has been added at the end of the break. Read the break from the reconciliation system again and draft again in the light of the reply.

ways: Entered by a member of the reconciliation team (the form at the top of the list)
Sent by the bank's reconciliation run for every unmatched item, or by its event for a new break (POST /api/intake with X-Intake-Token)

fields.label: Title of the break
fields.hint: The correspondent bank and what the item is, with the currency, for example Quenmark National Bank, statement debit USD 3,275.40.

fields.label: Unmatched entry
fields.hint: The entry id of the item the break is about, for example STM-8101 or LED-7402.

fields.label: Side of the unmatched entry
fields.hint: Which side the unmatched entry is on.

fields.label: Amount
fields.hint: The amount and whether it is a credit or a debit.

fields.label: Break opened on
fields.hint: The day the reconciliation run opened the break.

fields.label: Age of the break
fields.hint: How long it has been open, for example 9 days.

fields.label: Past a limit
fields.hint: Filled in by the reconciliation system when the break is past the limit of its rule, for example Over the 5-day limit. Leave it empty otherwise.

fields.label: What the desk knows of the break

draft.instruction:
An item is unmatched after a reconciliation run at the bank's reconciliation desk. Work on the break named in the case below. Gather both sides, examine each candidate entry, and propose the match or the adjusting entry, with the evidence and the matching rule you relied on. You post nothing and reverse nothing: a person approves every posting. Where the break cannot be resolved, say so, list what was checked, and refer it to a person. Read the break, with its candidates, the checks the automatic matcher already ran and the matching rules, from the reconciliation system before you write anything. Read each entry you rely on, ledger or statement: its record shows which breaks name it. Then search the ledger and the statement entries to prove what you say: that a match is the only one, that an entry is not repeated, or that nothing exists. Search by account, amount, value dates and reference. A search that finds nothing is a finding, and so is a search that finds only entries that do not belong. Say for every search what you gave it and what it found. Use only entry ids the system returns. Every statement carries an entry id and the rule. Never match to make the books balance: if no entry could belong to the item, do not match it, do not write it off and do not adjust. Never reverse an entry that is matched to a statement entry. Reply in this shape and in no other. Write plain statements. Do not write in the first person. Write every date as day, short month and year, for example 21 Nov 2026, never as 2026-11-21 and never as a number of days ago. Write every amount with two decimals and a comma for thousands, then credit or debit, for example 12,480.00 credit. Give the difference between two amounts with its working, for example 25,000.00 less 24,962.50 is 37.50, and the difference between two dates in days. 1. The heading "Summary", then the lines described below, with no blank line between them. The last of them starts "Saved:" and says whether the draft proposal was saved to the reconciliation system, and as which version, using only what the system's reply said. If the system refused, give what it said. If you did not try to save, say so. 2. A blank line, then the heading "Draft proposal. For the reconciliation analyst. Not issued." 3. A Markdown table with exactly these seven columns and no other. Put no vertical bar inside a cell. | # | Examined | The item | Compared with | Ids and rule | Mark | Note | # is 1, 2, 3 in order. Examined says what the row is: the unmatched item, a candidate entry ("Ledger entry LED-7101"), or a search or a check that found nothing or found only entries that do not belong, with what was given to it. The item and Compared with are written in the same form, so that the two can be read against each other: one line for each part, separated by
, each starting with its label and a colon, in this order: "Entry:" the entry id with its side and account in brackets, for example LED-7101 (ledger, NOS-ALDB-01); "Amount:" the currency, the amount, then credit or debit, for example USD 12,480.00 credit; "Date:" the value date; "Reference:" the reference; then "Narrative:" when the entry has one, and "Batch:" when it has a batch, with the posting time. The item is the break item. Compared with is the candidate, or what the search found. Write the currency before the amount. Where a search found nothing, or found only the item itself, the row has one box: write the same text in The item and in Compared with, "No entry found" (or "Only STM-8501, the item itself"). Name a search by what it was given: "Ledger search for the amount USD 3,275.40, any account, any date". When both ends of a range are the same figure, write the figure once and never "from 3,275.40 to 3,275.40"; keep "from ... to ..." for a real range such as value dates. Ids and rule is the entry ids and the rule the row rests on, separated by semicolons. Mark is exactly one of: unmatched, matches, differs, no counterpart, in lower case. Note says why, with the difference in amount (with its working) or in days, or the minutes between two posting times, and the rule. Write one row for the unmatched item first. In that row The item holds the item in full, with its entry id, side and account, and its narrative after the reference, and Compared with holds exactly "No matched entry yet". Then one row for each candidate the system lists, then one row for each search or check that found nothing or found only entries that do not belong. Marks: unmatched for the item the break is about; matches when the entry belongs with it under a rule, and say which; differs when the entry was examined and does not belong, and say why; no counterpart when a search or a check found nothing on the other side to compare with, and say what was searched for. 4. A blank line, then one line that starts "Proposal:". Write nothing after it. Summary lines, at most six, and no count of marks (the desk counts them from the table): the break id, the account and the unmatched item (entry id, amount, date, side) and the day the break was opened; which candidate entries match and why, and which do not; the rule relied on; the amount difference, if there is one; the searches made, each with what it found; then the "Saved:" line. Where a match needs no adjusting entry, say in the Summary in these words that no adjusting entry is needed. When you list the checks the matcher ran, call the check for an entry posted twice the duplicate check. The "Proposal:" line starts with exactly one of: "approve the match"; "approve the match and the adjusting entry"; "approve the reversal"; or "refer to a person". Straight after it comes a colon and the kind of break in a few words (for example mistyped reference, one statement credit for a batch, bank charge, duplicate posting, no counterpart), and a full stop. That first sentence is shown to the analyst first, so keep it short and put no other full stop in it. Then say what it concerns: for a match, the item, the entries it matches and the rule; for a match with an adjusting entry, also the account to debit, the account to credit and the amount; for a reversal, the duplicate entry, the entry it duplicates and the rule, and that the other entry is not reversed; for a referral, the rule, the role the rule sends the break to, how old the break is and what was checked and searched. Never write that anything has been posted.

markHints.unmatched: The item the break is about
markHints.matches: The entry belongs with the break item under a matching rule
markHints.differs: The entry was examined and does not belong with the break item
markHints.no counterpart: A search was made and found nothing on the other side to compare with. That is a finding, not a failure

decisions.label: Approve the proposal
decisions.hint: Records that you approve version {version}{edited} of the proposal, in your name: the match, the adjusting entry or the reversal. It posts nothing and changes no entry. A person with the authority posts it in the reconciliation system.

decisions.label: Refer to the team lead
decisions.noteLabel: Why it goes to the team lead, and what was checked
decisions.noteHint: The matching rules send a break that has no candidate to the Reconciliation Team lead, and the same day when the break is older than five days.

decisions.label: Ask the agent to redo the proposal
decisions.noteLabel: What the agent got wrong or missed (it sees this note)

register.heading: Every decision and every removal, in the order it was taken. The desk posts no match, writes off nothing and reverses no entry: a person does that in the reconciliation system.

rules.fourEyesText: The person who entered a break cannot decide it. Any other reconciliation analyst can. You can still ask the agent to redo the proposal.

next.issued: Recorded as approved. Nothing further happens on this desk. The match, the adjusting entry or the reversal is posted in the reconciliation system by the person who has the authority.
next.referred: Recorded as referred to the team lead, with the reason you gave. The decision is theirs.

decisionLabels.sent_back: Asked the agent to redo the proposal
